Title: One more call for Urdu Translation Project.

Body.Text:
RA needed for Urdu translation

Undergrads are welcome to follow up on this position if interested. This is a limited duration through the mid-September 2026.
We are looking for one more paid research assistant fluent in Urdu to translate the text of advertisements from newspapers published in 1950s Delhi.
An ideal RA will be meticulous and accurate and able to maintain quality across a large quantity of, often repetitive, text.
Experience with historical research and knowledge of contextual literary and cultural references are desirable but not required.

Pay will be hourly @ $15/hr. The work can be carried out at your own pace within a stipulated time period.
If interested, please contact Dr. Anish Vanaik (avanaik@purdue.edu).

Title: Research Opportunity: AI in Healthcare Intervention Design

Body.Text:
Project Overview: We are seeking highly motivated undergraduate research assistants to join an interdisciplinary team developing a novel, AI-driven healthcare intervention. The project focuses on refining a conversational mHealth (AI) tool designed to support adults in managing chronic conditions, specifically targeting cardiovascular and metabolic health through lifestyle and dietary guidance.
This project operates at the intersection of clinical science and artificial intelligence. Students will have the opportunity to contribute to the foundational design and refinement phases of a tool intended for eventual clinical deployment.
What You Will Do: Depending on your background and interests, tasks may include:

For Technical Tracks: Assisting with the refinement of Large Language Model (LLM) components, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, or improving the front-end user interface of the chatbot.
For Clinical/Design Tracks: Curating and organizing evidence-based clinical resources, assisting with Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) design principles, and supporting the preparation of early-stage user feedback studies.

Who We Are Looking For: We welcome students from both technical (Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science) and clinical/biological (Nursing, Pre-Med, Public Health, Nutrition, biological science, etc.) backgrounds.
Relevant experience in any of the following is valued:

Python programming, web development, or AI/NLP systems.
Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) or user experience (UX) design.
Knowledge of nutrition, chronic disease management, or public health.
Note: Students with strong clinical or health sciences backgrounds are highly encouraged to apply, even without extensive programming experience.

Why Join?

Academic Credit: Opportunities are available for 1-credit research course enrollment for the Summer term, with the potential for continuation into the Fall based on performance and project needs.
Real-World Impact: Gain hands-on experience in the rapidly growing field of digital health and AI-enabled clinical tools.

How to Apply: If you are interested, please send a brief email to Dr. Ding’s team (pdresearch@purdue.edu) introducing yourself, your major, your availability during the summer and why you are interested in this intersection of AI and healthcare. Please attach your resume or CV detailing any relevant skills or coursework.

Title: Graduate study opportunity for seniors graduating this and next semester – IE Build@Scale Lab

Body.Text:
Professor Wenzhuo Wu (Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering) is recruiting highly motivated students to join the IE Build@Scale Lab as graduate students starting in Summer or Fall 2026.
The lab is launching a new initiative focused on an AI-empowered manufacturing framework—integrating augmented reality, robotics, digital twins, wearable sensing, and AI to support advanced manufacturing and prototyping, as well as new research and curriculum development.
Areas of interest include:

Robotics and embedded systems
AI / machine learning / LLM frameworks (Python, PyTorch, LangChain, etc.)
AR/VR development (Unity, VisionOS, RealityKit, Apple Vision Pro, etc.)
Digital twins and simulation (Omniverse, ROS, control systems)
Advanced manufacturing (CNC, additive manufacturing, laser processing)
Human–computer interaction or sensor systems

Application details:

Final deadline for domestic applicants (with potential RA support): May 30, 2026
Start term: Summer or Fall 2026 (flexible)

Interested students are encouraged to reach out directly to Dr. Wu (wu966@purdue.edu) to discuss their interest. He will help coordinate the application process with the IE graduate office.

Title: Research Opportunity:  JMHC Afterschool Needs Assessment and Strategic Planning

Body.Text:
Title: JMHC Afterschool Needs Assessment and Strategic Planning
Research Area: Education, Youth Development, Mixed Methods, Longitudinal
Term: AY 2026-2027
Mentor: Dr. Temitope F. Olenloa, JMHC Clinical Assistant Professor, adeoye@purdue.edu
Websites: https://linktr.ee/headsupgl
Description: The Heads Up Tutoring & Life Skills program is an afterschool program in east Lafayette. We support K-12 youth in Greater Lafayette by providing homework help, mentoring, and summer enrichment opportunities. This community-based research project partners with Heads Up to analyze survey, focus group, and grade reflection forms to support Heads Up in developing a strategic plan and program redesign. Dr. Adeoye Olenloa is currently recruiting undergraduate students interested in gaining longitudinal, mixed (qualitative and quantitative) research skills.
Type of work required: There is room to propose research questions, engage in data collection and analysis, publish and present research in academic venues, and create a scholarly project with this research.
Qualifications: Interested students will need to pass a registry check (for violent and sexual offenders). Accepted students will attend homework help or other Heads Up sessions at least once per month to get familiar with the community. Looking for JMHC undergraduate researchers only for this position but any student can volunteer with the lab so email Dr. Temi (adeoye@purdue.edu) if interested but not a JMHC student.
This project is offered under the OUR Scholar Program. Eligible JMHC students may receive a $1,000 scholarship ($500 per semester), co-sponsored by the Office of Undergraduate Research (OUR) and JMHC. More information can be found on OUR website.
Program Eligibility criteria:

Applicants must commit to participating in the project for a minimum of two semesters- Fall 2026 and Spring 2027.
Applicants must NOT have a prior scholarly project on record and commit to completing a scholarly project through participation in this program.
Students who have previously received funding through the OUR Scholar Program are not eligible to apply.

To apply, please go to the OURConnect, under OUR Scholars- John Martinson Honors College Program.

Title: PURC Is This Week! Join the JMHC Green Room on April 14

Body.Text:
The Purdue Undergraduate Research Conference (PURC) is taking place this week! As the largest showcase of undergraduate research at Purdue, PURC highlights outstanding student scholarship across disciplines.
Whether you are considering pursuing your own research project or simply want to broaden your academic perspective, this conference offers a great opportunity to explore cutting-edge research, gain new insights, and engage with presenters while networking with peers.
Attached, you will find a list of JMHC presenters and their presentation details in the Division key and the abstract book.
Join us in the Green Room tomorrow, April 14! A Green Room will be available in STEW 202 from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM during the in-person poster sessions. Feel free to stop by anytime to prepare, relax, connect with peers, or show your support. Space to store your belongings and refreshments will be provided.
We look forward to seeing you there!

Title: 2026-2027 OUR Scholar Program Research Opportunity- StreamCI Integration for Ecological Data

Body.Text:
Title: StreamCI Integration for Ecological Data
Research Area: Computer Science, Cyberinfrastructure, Ecology, Conservation
Term: AY 2026-2027
Mentor: Dr. Kristen Marie Bellisario, JMHC Clinical Assistant Professor, kbellisa@purdue.edu 
Description: This project situates undergraduate research within the NSF-funded National Science Foundation Cyberinfrastructure for Sustained Scientific Innovation (CSSI) initiative, StreamCI, which aims to enable scalable, AI-ready data pipelines for scientific applications. As a participating domain science, our goal is to adapt unstructured ecological datasets—particularly acoustic recordings and camera trap imagery—for integration into the StreamCI framework. These data are central to ongoing conservation efforts focused on species such as the bobcat, gray wolf, and American black bear, where large volumes of sensor data are collected but remain difficult to standardize and analyze at scale. Enabling these data within StreamCI supports a broader “Conservation in Action” goal: transforming raw environmental observations into actionable ecological insight.
Type of work required: The undergraduate researcher will play a central role in transforming unstructured ecological data into structured, machine-readable formats suitable for streaming data pipelines. This includes examining raw datasets to identify patterns, inconsistencies, and missing metadata; defining appropriate data fields and schema; and evaluating how these design choices affect downstream analysis.
A key component of the project is student-driven inquiry. The researcher will develop an independent research question related to data representation, selection, or preprocessing in ecological monitoring systems. They will select datasets, implement data transformations, and test how different schema and preprocessing strategies influence the performance of analytical or algorithmic workflows within StreamCI.Through this work, the student will contribute to enabling multimodal ecological data (audio and imagery) to function effectively within a national cyberinfrastructure platform. The project advances both domain-specific knowledge in ecological informatics and broader goals of reproducible, scalable data science in support of wildlife conservation.
Qualifications: Experience coding in R or Python (coursework is great!) Interest in conservation, wildlife, or environmental data Interest in working with both data and field-based research teams
This project is offered under the OUR Scholar Program. Eligible JMHC students may receive a $1,000 scholarship ($500 per semester), co-sponsored by the Office of Undergraduate Research (OUR) and JMHC. More information can be found on OUR website.
Program eligibility criteria:

Applicants must commit to participating in the project for a minimum of two semesters- Fall 2026 and Spring 2027.
Applicants must NOT have a prior scholarly project on record and commit to completing a scholarly project through participation in this program.
Students who have previously received funding through the OUR Scholar Program are not eligible to apply.

To apply, please go to the OURConnect, under OUR Scholars- John Martinson Honors College Program.
